title: Results From The 124 Of The 200 Games For The AI Game Festival
author: bingewavecinema
selftext:
124 games have applied so for the [AI Gaming Festival ](https://www.glitch.fun/gameshows/9eadde86-a1b2-4882-86e4-a3e9e2e08814/view/standalone)(submissions are still open until the end of this month). Our goal is 200 games and there is the $20k Token Grant for developers.

I just want to share some of the results of how people are using AI. Artwork (capsule art, website art, etc) is what is most used, following by programming and asset creation (sprite, textures, etc).

Here are a list of one of use cases:

1. Background game music
2. Balancing spells, synergies, and mutations
3. Music and SFX
4. Video AI assistance for character and cartridge visuals
5. A local LLM classifying player input
6. AI-assisted “Literal Illusions” puzzle development
7. Neural networks learning from player behavior for asynchronous PvP
8. Animation
9. Creating development pipelines to help a solo developer scale production
10. AI assistance for nearly everything
11. AI-generated scene backgrounds
12. Ideas for levels
13. Runtime LLM inference allowing players to customize game systems, features, and story

One thing is very interesting too; we're getting sponsors and free credits and swag to other AI services, many that seem to be struggling to get users. Its either that developers are only using 1 to 2 LLMs (Claude and OpenAI) that is doing the job of the other services or people just don't now the other developers exist.

comments.author: perrinashcroft
comments.body:
People selling all these AI middleware services are going to struggle because the beauty of AI is that if I need some random tool or workflow I'm missing I can vibe code exactly what i want myself, rather than paying a subscription to try using someone else's vibe coded attempt at the problem. 

Even if I liked what they're doing I'd rather build my own that I could maintain and customise rather than just hoping they don't get bored and shut it all down. Most of these AI services are going to be gone in 6-12 months when the creator finds they're not taking off, to be replaced by a new wave of them.

There's no shortage of people trying to sell pickaxes during a gold rush, but this is gold rush where we've all been given a butler who'll make whatever pickaxes or tools we want.

replies.author: Onye_Nacho
replies.body:
That is why I personally despise subscriptions scams (even GAI ones) and always encourage FOSS alternatives. Unless it is a FOSS option that I can use for free without relying on a service whence the provider can just suddenly off it all and fuck me over, I don't care about anymore MS-GAI tools.

**Note**: MS = Mainstream.

comments.author: Onye_Nacho
comments.body: Right now, I am looking for a FOSS alternative to topologize 3D models from high poly down to low poly. If anyone knows what tool can do that FREE AND OPEN-SOURCE, let me know.

replies.author: OGMajinNuub
replies.body: Blender decimation is alright, would require slight work after but most of it can be done with claude using blender MCP. Zbrush has their Zremesher tool (what i use and recommend), and meshy.ai has a retop/Remesh feature i believe can be done on models you provide but it worked OK and it costs credits. Zbrush has a free version for IPAD if you have one that includes the Zremesher which for me would be the best option if you want good results, good topology.

replies.author: Onye_Nacho
replies.body:
(\*sigh\*) I will stress the following statement I have said earlier:

>If anyone knows what tool can do that **FREE AND OPEN-SOURCE**, let me know.

Anything that costs money (worse of all, a subscription service) is effectively useless to me. I am already familiar with Meshy and was quite annoyed by their greedy subscription scam service of which won't even let me download the models I created less I pay them money. I'll never have interest in investing in such services. The very nature of Meshy reeks with shadiness and petty limitations.  


Claude is also limited by a subscription service, but at least it seems to grant me more freedom via the free tier.  


Blender MCP is thus far the sole outlier from your response that might be considerable for me.  
If all else fails, guess I'll just recreate the mesh from scratch or manually retopologize it...

replies.author: OGMajinNuub
replies.body: As I said. Zbrush has a free version for IPad that does exactly what you want 100% to a T with just a couple clicks of the interface, so if you dont think that applies so be it. I've used Meshy. I think paying less than $.50 a model is negligible for what you are getting back. Meshy also gives ridiculous amounts of free tokens.. so free generations, and downloads don't use tokens. With claude MCP you never even have to go to the meshy website its all handle by claude in app. If you choose to go the manual route, you are paying with your time a far more valuable resource. Best of luck to you. Hope you find what you're looking for.

replies.body: I will check out these options. Is there not a PC version of this retopology feature in ZBrush? I do not own/have an IPad.

replies.body: Yes. But its not free like the iPad version.
